The app's Export step writes one folder per export group containing everything you
need to submit your records to GenBank: the sequences (with customized FASTA headers),
feature tables, and a summary of the checks. This page helps you understand the
GenBank submission process. The
[Export walkthrough](Test-Project-Export.html) shows the Export step itself.

# Which files to upload

For rRNA and ITS sequences, NCBI's Submission Portal
(https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov) takes a FASTA file only. Upload
`<group>.fasta`. The Portal finds the genes itself with ITSx, and writes its own
annotation, so the `.tbl` feature tables are not used there.

The Portal rewrites definition lines in its own wording (small and large subunit
ribosomal RNA), so the 18S and 28S wording in your file will not survive.

# The FASTA header template

Each record's FASTA header comes from a template. The default is:

```
{seqid} [organism={organism}] [moltype=genomic DNA] {organism} {rrna_definition}
```

and the default for the per-marker files is:

```
{seqid}_{element} [organism={organism}] {organism} {product}
```

Edit them in the **Export Data** window. Each template is checked as you type,
and **Save template** keeps it under a name, so a lab can keep one per
submission style. Words in braces are filled in for each record:

| Token | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `{seqid}` | The record's name: the sample ID, or `<ID>_p<path>_s<contig>` when the sample gives more than one record. Keep it in every template. |
| `{organism}` | The organism name to submit (see below). |
| `{rrna_definition}` | The definition phrase, for example "18S ribosomal RNA gene, partial sequence; internal transcribed spacer 1, 5.8S ribosomal RNA gene, and internal transcribed spacer 2, complete sequence; and 28S ribosomal RNA gene, partial sequence." |
| `{completeness}` | "complete sequence" or "partial sequence", for the record as a whole. |
| `{elements}` | The features in order, for example `18S-ITS1-5.8S-ITS2-28S`. |
| `{length}`, `{n_features}`, `{missing}` | Record length, number of features, and missing features. |
| `{sci_name}`, `{taxid}` | The name and NCBI taxon ID set in the Taxonomy step. |
| `{element}`, `{product}` | Per-marker template only: the marker (18S, ITS1, and so on) and its product name. |

Any column of your mapping file works too, as `{ColumnName}`. The
**Your mapping columns** chips in the Export Data window show every name you
can use. You can also use metadata imported from GEOME, GBIF, or NCBI. 
See [Sample metadata](Sample-Metadata.html#using-metadata-fields-at-export).

# Required source modifiers

For each rDNA sequences, GenBank requires the organism name, one identifier for the
sample (isolate, strain, clone, or specimen voucher), the collection date, and
where it was collected. Add them to your template as source modifiers:
`[specimen_voucher=...]`, `[collection_date=...]`, and `[geo_loc_name=...]`.
NCBI's full list is
[Modifiers for FASTA Definition Lines](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genbank/mods_fastadefline/).

For example, with `Voucher`, `Date`, and `Country` columns in your mapping file:

```
{seqid} [organism={organism}] [specimen_voucher={Voucher}] [collection_date={Date}] [geo_loc_name={Country}] [moltype=genomic DNA] {organism} {rrna_definition}
```

Instead of including these values as columns in your mapping file, you can fetch them from GEOME,
GBIF, or NCBI BioSample. The **Export** column of the **Metadata** button offers
ready-made values such as `{geome_lat_lon}` and `{gbif_collection_date}`, which
you place in the template yourself. Smithsonian NMNH specimens also need a
`voucherURI`; see [NMNH voucher submissions](NMNH-Vouchers.html).

If a record would get an empty modifier, such as `[collection_date=]` for a
sample with no date, the template check warns and names the records. NCBI does
not accept an empty modifier: fill in the column, or use one of NCBI's accepted
missing-value terms, such as `missing` or `not collected`. If you continue with 
export, missing metadata in the FASTA header will be removed on a sample-by-sample basis.

# The organism name

`{organism}` is the name confirmed in the Taxonomy step. If the Taxonomy step
did not result in an exact match, `{organism}` is set to the Taxon label from
your map file, so an informal name such as "Upeneus sp. A" is
kept. To always use your own label, put `{Taxon}` in the template instead.

When your map file Taxon differs from the name set in the Taxonomy step, the record's
`submission_risk` column says `taxon_differs(<name>)`, so you can check which
one you want.

# Samples with more than one record

When a sample has more than one contig at export, RiboPilot adds `[isolate=<ID>_p<path>_s<contig>]` 
to each FASTA header. This allows GenBank to differentiate records that share an
organism and a voucher number. 

For that reason, a template with its own `[isolate=...]` is refused for an
export group that contains a sample with multiple contigs. It is allowed otherwise.

# Complete or partial

Since GenBank performs its own annotation, the following information can usually
be ignored for the submission process.

The end of a gene is written as partial (`<` for the 5' end or `>` for the 3' end in
the feature table, and "partial sequence" in the definition line) when:

- it runs into the end of a contig that has not been trimmed (the gene ran
  off the assembled contig)
- the quality check found the gene truncated, meaning less than 90 percent of
  it was recovered. The end that meets no neighbouring spacer or gene is marked
  if both ends meet one, both are marked
- a trim cut through the gene. A trim that lands on a gene boundary marks
  nothing

Your own choice always wins: the **5'** and **3'** buttons under **Partial** in
the contig window (check **Edit**, pick the feature, then **Save**) can be used 
to override RiboPilot. **Mark Partial** on the contig only changes `{completeness}` to "partial
sequence"; it does not mark any gene end.

# Flanking sequence

Contigs often contain sequence beyond the core rDNA region. This is intergenic spacer (IGS):
5' external transcribed spacer (ETS) before the 18S, and its 3'
ETS after the 28S. RiboPilot
does not annotate these flanks, and GenBank tends to reject submissions containing sequences
containing IGS/ETS. We recommend that you trim contigs to gene boundaries before export.

# Gaps inside a record

A run of 10 or more N bases counts as a gap. NCBI may remove a record with a
gap inside the 18S-to-28S region; the `gap_in_rDNA` flag below marks these.

# Check before you submit

After export, the summary files note samples that have submission-risk flags.
However, some warning messages may also appear during the export process.

**Flagged records.** Before it writes anything, the Export window lists every
contig that the BLAST screen or the chimera check flagged, and that you
have not marked "Reviewed". You can choose to **Leave them out** or  **Export anyway**.

**The final ITSx check.** NCBI runs a standard ITSx check on every rRNA and ITS
submission. It may suggest that you remove records judged chimeric, gapped, or misassembled by ITSx.
RiboPilot runs the same check on your records after writing them. The result is printed at export and
recorded in the `itsx_check` column of `<group>_summary.csv` and in
`<group>_itsx_check.csv`. It only warns: nothing is removed.

**The submission_risk column.** Each record's row in `<group>_summary.csv` lists
any of these flags:

| Flag | What it means |
|---|---|
| `chimeric(...)` | Parts of the sequence match different phyla or kingdoms (a severe chimera call); the reason is in brackets. |
| `chimeric(ITSx)` | ITSx calls the record chimeric. |
| `gap_in_rDNA` | A run of N bases falls between the start of the 18S and the end of the 28S. |
| `misassembly` | Features overlap or are out of order. |
| `off_target(<taxon>)` | The BLAST screen's hits agree on a taxon that is not on the sample's lineage. |
| `contaminant` | The BLAST screen's best hit is from a different phylum than the sample. |
| `taxon_differs(<name>)` | Your Taxon differs from the name set in the Taxonomy step. |
| `missing_organism` | The record has no organism name. |

Check `off_target` and `contaminant` records before you submit: the sequence may
be another organism's rDNA, exported under your sample's name. Weaker chimera
evidence is in the separate `chimera_warning` column; it is not a submission
risk, but it is worth a look in the app.

# What is in the export folder

```
out/export/<group>/
    <group>.fasta           every record, one file (this is what you upload)
    <group>.tbl             feature tables (for your records; not uploaded)
    <group>_summary.csv     one row per record, with submission_risk
    <group>_report.html     review report with feature maps and alignments
    <group>_itsx_check.csv  what stock ITSx says about each record
    README.txt              how to submit
    samples/                one .fasta and .tbl per record
    markers/                one folder per marker (18S, ITS1, and so on)
    itsx_check/             raw ITSx output behind the check
```

The summary CSV also says which records are variants of each other, in the
`variant_class`, `variant_group`, `variant_identity`, and `n_variants` columns;
see [Quality checks and flags](Curation-Flags.html).
